action_criteria.expected_evidence: MoCA 17/30 with delayed recall 0/5 not helped by cueing or recognition, executive losses, and informant FAQ 22/30
action_criteria.label: Perform a validated bedside cognitive assessment and record the per-domain profile and whether delayed recall improves with cueing
action_criteria.rationale: A post-stroke decline with an informant history of earlier memory loss needs a validated screen with cued and recognition recall to separate a storage amnesia from a retrieval deficit.

action_criteria.expected_evidence: Delayed recall below the 1st and recognition at the 4th percentile with Trail Making B 6th and SDMT 8th percentile
action_criteria.label: Order formal multi-domain neuropsychological testing to settle the executive-versus-amnestic attribution and to document a baseline for follow-up
action_criteria.rationale: Formal testing documents an amnestic storage deficit alongside dysexecutive slowing, the two components a mixed attribution needs.

action_criteria.expected_evidence: TSH, B12, folate, RPR, HIV and CBC normal; HbA1c 8.2% on metformin and gliclazide; eGFR 58; LDL 92 mg/dL on rosuvastatin 20 mg
action_criteria.label: Order the reversible-cause screen and the vascular-risk assays that will be treated (CBC, CMP, TSH, B12, folate, HbA1c, lipid panel)
action_criteria.rationale: Reversible contributors must be excluded, and the glycaemic, renal and lipid values set his diabetes and secondary-prevention plan.

action_criteria.expected_evidence: Chronic left VPL thalamic lacune and two further lacunes, Fazekas 2, no microbleeds, Scheltens MTA 3 bilaterally with temporoparietal atrophy
action_criteria.label: Obtain brain MRI reported in STRIVE-2 terms (lacunes, white matter grade, DWI, SWI) with the medial temporal atrophy grade
action_criteria.rationale: MRI localises the index lacune and grades both the vascular burden and the medial temporal atrophy that points to a second process.

action_criteria.expected_evidence: Sinus rhythm at 70 bpm with LVH by voltage; no atrial fibrillation
action_criteria.label: Obtain a 12-lead ECG to look for atrial fibrillation as the embolic source and for the left ventricular hypertrophy of chronic hypertension
action_criteria.rationale: After an ischaemic stroke the ECG documents rhythm, and it is the baseline before a cholinesterase inhibitor.

action_criteria.expected_evidence: Right ICA less than 30% and left ICA 30-40% stenosis; no significant stenosis
action_criteria.label: Image the extracranial carotid arteries if not already done at the stroke admission
action_criteria.rationale: A lacunar infarct was worked up at admission; repeat carotid imaging is defensible but changes little.

action_criteria.expected_evidence: CSF Abeta42 402 pg/mL, ratio 0.048, phospho-tau181 84 pg/mL, or a positive amyloid PET
action_criteria.label: Establish amyloid status with one biomarker (CSF Abeta42/40 with phospho-tau, or amyloid PET): whether Alzheimer pathology coexists with the vascular burden
action_criteria.rationale: A storage-type amnesia, Scheltens 3 atrophy and a pre-stroke decline make coexisting Alzheimer pathology the question; one amyloid biomarker answers it.

action_criteria.expected_evidence: Gliclazide with perindopril raises hypoglycaemia risk at eGFR 58; donepezil has no interacting drug on his list
action_criteria.label: Review his medicines for hypoglycaemia risk (gliclazide) and check any cholinesterase inhibitor against them
action_criteria.rationale: He takes a sulfonylurea while unable to recognise hypoglycaemia, and a cholinesterase inhibitor is likely to be started.

prohibited_recommendations: Do not attribute everything to the stroke when the informant describes two years of decline before it.
Do not attribute everything to Alzheimer's disease and omit secondary prevention for a documented lacunar stroke.
Do not continue a sulfonylurea in a patient who cannot reliably recognise or report hypoglycaemia [ADA_older_adults_2026].
Do not accept a thalamic lacune as the explanation for a storage-type amnesia without asking which nucleus was involved.
Do not prescribe anticholinergic medications alongside a cholinesterase inhibitor.
required_recommendations: Explain to Mr Sanna and his daughter that this is mixed dementia: Alzheimer disease that began before the stroke, with a vascular step from the thalamic lacune on a background of small-vessel disease [VASCOG_2014].
Offer a cholinesterase inhibitor for the Alzheimer component (e.g. donepezil 5 mg at night, increased to 10 mg after 4-6 weeks if tolerated), with pulse checked at each step.

Stop gliclazide and individualise the HbA1c target to about below 8.0% (currently 8.2% on metformin and gliclazide), using an agent with low hypoglycaemia risk if more control is needed [ADA_older_adults_2026].
Continue clopidogrel 75 mg daily as single antiplatelet therapy after the lacunar stroke [AHA_ASA_2021_secondary].
Lower blood pressure gradually to below 130/80 mmHg (currently 150/82 mmHg), checking orthostatic BP at each change given his fall [AHA_ASA_2021_secondary].

Intensify lipid lowering to LDL below 55 mg/dL (current 92 mg/dL on rosuvastatin 20 mg, with carotid plaque): very high risk after an ischaemic stroke at 79 with hypertension and diabetes; add ezetimibe or increase the statin [ACC_AHA_dyslipidemia_2026].
Arrange carer support and supervision: medicines dispensed by his daughter or carers, home gas safety after two incidents, and advance care planning while he can contribute.

avoided_actions.rationale: EEG has no diagnostic role here: the course is a slow decline with one stroke-related step, with no fluctuation, episodes or rapid progression.

A presynaptic dopaminergic study answers the Lewy-body question, not the vascular one, and there is no spontaneous parkinsonism, no fluctuating cognition with hallucinations and no REM sleep behaviour disorder
No parkinsonism, fluctuation, hallucinations or dream enactment: cardiac sympathetic imaging is a Lewy-body test with no question to answer here.
Two years of slow decline with one stroke-related step, not a subacute multidomain syndrome: a paraneoplastic or autoimmune-encephalitis battery has no indication.
MRI is available and not contraindicated; CT cannot show microbleeds, siderosis or small lacunes.
A lacunar thalamic infarct with two further lacunes, worked up at admission: there is no cortical or multi-territory infarct for a cardiac source to explain.
Lacunar small-vessel infarcts with sinus rhythm on 48 hours of telemetry and on the ECG; prolonged monitoring does not change management.

accepted: Mixed Alzheimer and vascular dementia: pre-existing Alzheimer's disease with a superimposed post-stroke step after a left thalamic lacunar infarct, on a background of moderate small-vessel disease

differential.key_features: The temporal criterion is satisfied and the step at the stroke is real, but the informant documents two years of amnestic decline before it, the amnesia is storage-type with impaired recognition, medial temporal atrophy is Scheltens 3 and the amyloid biomarker is positive; a ventral posterolateral thalamic lacune does not produce this

The biomarker and the atrophy establish Alzheimer pathology, but they do not explain the abrupt step at the stroke or the sensory deficit, and three lacunes with Fazekas 2 are a vascular contribution in their own right
The lacune is in the ventral posterolateral nucleus, a sensory relay, not in the anterior or paramedian nuclei that produce amnesia
Eleven weeks after the event with stable alertness, no fluctuation and no precipitant
No fluctuation, hallucinations, spontaneous parkinsonism or dream enactment

key_clinical_evidence: The temporal criterion for post-stroke dementia is satisfied here, and it is still not the whole diagnosis: a documented pre-stroke decline plus a storage-type amnesia plus Scheltens 3 atrophy plus a positive amyloid biomarker make this mixed disease

Nucleus matters: a ventral posterolateral thalamic lacune produces contralateral sensory loss, whereas amnesia requires the anterior or paramedian nuclei — so the index lesion cannot account for the memory deficit
Impaired recognition memory is the finding that forces the second diagnosis, because it marks storage rather than retrieval failure
Mixed disease is a diagnosis, not a hedge, and it has two treatment implications rather than one
Hypoglycaemia in a patient who cannot recognise or report it is itself a cause of cognitive harm, which makes the sulfonylurea a target of the assessment

red_herrings.correct_interpretation: The stroke did produce a step, but two years of pre-stroke amnestic decline, a storage-type amnesia, Scheltens 3 atrophy and a positive amyloid biomarker establish a coexisting degenerative process
red_herrings.data_point: A documented stroke eleven weeks before presentation
red_herrings.intended_effect: Satisfies the temporal criterion and closes the diagnosis as post-stroke vascular dementia, leaving the Alzheimer component untreated

red_herrings.correct_interpretation: The lacune is in the ventral posterolateral nucleus, a sensory relay; the amnesic thalamic syndrome requires the anterior or paramedian nuclei and the mamillothalamic tract
red_herrings.data_point: A thalamic infarct, a site known to cause amnesia
red_herrings.intended_effect: Explains the dense amnesia as a strategic thalamic syndrome and stops the search

sequence_constraints.reason: Document the cognitive deficit before attributing it: imaging read without a cognitive profile invites over-attribution of incidental white matter change
Exclude a mass lesion or lobar haemorrhage on MRI before a lumbar puncture.

interactions: Perindopril, amlodipine, rosuvastatin, clopidogrel, metformin, gliclazide: no clinically significant pharmacokinetic interaction.
donepezil.summary: No interacting drug on the current list; monitor heart rate for cholinergic bradycardia.
warnings: Cholinergic vagotonic effect: bradycardia, heart block and syncope; check pulse and ECG before and after dose increases (no current rate-limiting drug).
Gastrointestinal effects (nausea, diarrhoea, weight loss) are dose-related; start at 5 mg and increase after 4-6 weeks.
Avoid adding drugs with anticholinergic activity, which oppose its effect.

interactions: Perindopril: ACE inhibitors can enhance the glucose-lowering effect of sulfonylureas; hypoglycaemia risk increased.
Metformin: additive glucose lowering (intended); hypoglycaemia risk comes from the sulfonylurea.
Clopidogrel, rosuvastatin, amlodipine: no clinically significant interaction.
gliclazide.summary: Gliclazide with perindopril increases hypoglycaemia risk in an older adult with reduced renal function; agents with low hypoglycaemia risk are available.
warnings: Sulfonylureas carry the highest hypoglycaemia risk among oral agents in older adults, increased by reduced renal function (eGFR 58) and by cognitive impairment that prevents recognising or reporting symptoms.
Beers criteria: avoid sulfonylureas as first- or second-line therapy in older adults.

metadata.difficulty_rationale: Moderate: a satisfied temporal criterion invites a single vascular diagnosis, while the pre-stroke history, the storage-type amnesia, the atrophy grade and the biomarkers together establish mixed disease
key_educational_points: Post-stroke dementia and Alzheimer's disease frequently coexist, and the pre-stroke history is what reveals it
Thalamic nuclei have distinct syndromes; the sensory nuclei do not produce amnesia
Recognition memory testing distinguishes storage from retrieval failure and thereby the underlying pathology
Mixed disease carries two treatment plans, and omitting either is a failure of the diagnosis

patient.history_present_illness: Mr. Vittorio Sanna is a 79-year-old retired bank clerk who had a left thalamic lacunar infarct eleven weeks ago, presenting late with right hemibody sensory loss and mild right leg weakness. His daughter's history is more complicated than a simple post-stroke decline. She reports that for about two years before the stroke he had been forgetting conversations, losing objects and repeating himself; she had stopped his driving eighteen months ago for that reason, and had begun managing his bills. He was, however, still living alone, cooking, and taking his own medication. Since the stroke he has been unable to live alone: he cannot retain new information at all, has left the gas on twice, cannot manage medication, and has moved in with her. She is clear that both things are true: he was declining before, and the stroke produced a further large step. Her mother's side of the family has dementia in two members. He has no hallucinations, no fluctuation in alertness and no dream enactment. His diabetes has been poorly controlled for some years, and his blood pressure has run at 150-160 systolic since discharge.
